📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:24PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Alvotech ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 12, 2026, Alvotech (ALVO -0.71%) unveiled that full-year performance will trend toward the lower end of its guidance range of $650 million to $700 million in revenue. Resolved manufacturing slowdowns are clearing the way for higher product shipments, positioned to meet expanding global demand for biosimilars, which are lower-cost versions of complex biological drugs. Three takeaways from management clarify the road ahead for long-term investors.

Recent findings suggest that operational bottlenecks at the Reykjavik facility previously restricted product supply, but recent approvals from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for Process 2.0, an enhanced manufacturing process, allow the company to double production output without expanding physical plant footprint.

It has been revealed that management is expanding beyond traditional licensing deals by securing co-commercialization rights in the U.S. alongside partner Lotus Pharmaceutical, allowing the company to retain greater economic value from its proposed biosimilars to Imfinzi and Hemlibra.

Industry observers note that securing early regulatory submissions establishes a structural market advantage, and management made the first global biosimilar filing for high-dose Eylea, an eye disease therapy, alongside early filings for gastrointestinal drug Entyvio across the U.S. and Europe.

It has been revealed that commercial deliveries are accelerating as facility production rebounds, supporting management's outlook for higher product volume in the final quarter. Secondary supply partnerships with Lotte Biologics and Fujifilm Biotechnologies provide long-term operational flexibility across global markets.

With balance sheet debt reduction planned for the second half of 2027, management is focusing capital allocation on advancing pending regulatory approvals and executing key commercial partnerships.

    #142500. Industry News: 2 Dividend Stocks to Buy in November and 1 to Leave on the Shelf

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (756 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: 2 Dividend Stocks to Buy in November and 1 to Leave on the Shelf

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:25PM EST.
    • Altria's (MO +1.95%) 5.9% yield is very attractive, but don't rush out and buy the stock.
    • In a recent development, altria isn't at any risk of going bankrupt.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:25PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Altria Group ›.

    Altria's (MO +1.95%) 5.9% yield is very attractive, but don't rush out and buy the stock. You may be better off with McCormick's (MKC +1.67%) 4.1%, or even Procter & Gamble's (PG +0.44%) 2.5%. Here's why two of these stocks could be buys in November, and one is likely best left on the shelf.

    In a recent development, altria isn't at any risk of going bankrupt. And its dividend doesn't look particularly risky, either. For more aggressive dividend investors, it may be worth a closer look given its well-above-market 5.9% yield. However, you have to ask yourself why that yield is so high before you buy the stock.

    The answer is that Altria's combustible tobacco business, largely cigarettes, accounted for $5.4 billion of its $6.1 billion in revenues in the third quarter of 2026. That's 88% of the top line, which is a significant problem when you consider that the number of cigarettes and cigars the firm sold fell 2.9% in the quarter to 16.2 billion. In the third quarter of 2021, the company sold nearly 24.5 billion, indicating that this is a long-term trend. To be fair, Altria is working hard to diversify its business away from smokeable products, but given the uncertainty in the market today, thanks to geopolitical conflict, inflation, belt-tightening consumers, and AI volatility, why take on that kind of business risk?

    At the other end of the risk spectrum is Procter & Gamble, one of the world's largest consumer-staples makers. The company sells paper products, toiletries, and makeup, with its brands typically positioned at the high end of the market. While there is some trade-down risk in that market position, P&G has long focused on leading the consumer staples sector with innovation. The goal is to produce products that consumers are willing to pay more for because they get more from them.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Right now, P&G's 2.5% yield is well above the market's 1% and the consumer staples average of 2%. So you aren't skimping on yield to own this well-run tech giant. That mentioned, its price-to-sales and price-to-earnings ratios are roughly in line with their five-year averages, so you aren't getting a bargain price, either. However, given that P&G was able to increase its organic sales growth by a respectable 4% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 despite increasingly cost-conscious consumers, conservative dividend investors should probably give it a closer look.

    McCormick's risk profile is a bit harder to define, but the risk-versus-reward balance is likely tilted toward reward. The historically high 4.1% yield is a key part of the equation, indicating the stock is cheap today. That's backed up by the P/S and P/E ratios being below their five-year averages. As with Altria, however, you have to ask why McCormick's yield is so high and its valuation so cheap.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The answer is that McCormick is in the middle of acquiring Unilever's (UL +2.48%) food business. That will roughly double the tech giant's size and require it to take on significant debt. Those are risks, but the two companies' spice- and flavor-focused portfolios are complementary and offer cross-selling opportunities. And McCormick has a strong acquisition history, including meeting its post-merger deleveraging commitments. If you can handle a little uncertainty for a significant increase in yield, you may want to take a risk on McCormick as November draws to a close. Unlike Altria, whose business is contracting, McCormick's business looks set to get much bigger.

    Sources indicate that altria's core business has been in decline for years. While the company has managed to maintain a growing dividend during this period, most long-term dividend investors are probably best off avoiding it. Conservative types would be better off with an industry stalwart like P&G. And if you are willing to take on a little more risk, McCormick's pending acquisition could be an opportunity to buy a historically well-run company while it is attractively priced and offers a well-above-market yield.

    Industry observers note that on its fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 12, 2026, Spectrum Brands (SPB +0.17%) unveiled full-year financial results and highlighted a proposal by Empower Brands, its joint venture with Oaktree, to acquire consumer products company Helen of Troy.     Higher commodity prices, transportation rates, and fuel expenses create unexpected cost pressures as fiscal 2027 begins. Management prepares to counter these cost increases through internal factory automation and targeted price adjustments.

    The business enters the latest fiscal year with high fill rates, which measure the percentage of customer orders fulfilled on time, alongside liquid reserves to back growth plans.

    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) have both taken a beating, with their shares now trading roughly 36% and 39% below their 52-week highs, respectively.
    • With both companies still benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, could this sell-off present an opportunity for long-term investors?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Orford – Nov 26, 2026 at 7:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) have both taken a beating, with their shares now trading roughly 36% and 39% below their 52-week highs, respectively. But history suggests that corrections don't necessarily mark the end of a bull cycle.

    With both companies still benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, could this sell-off present an opportunity for long-term investors?

    According to recent reports, nvidia remains at the center of the AI boom, supplying the graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and software that power the world's largest data centers. That said, the recent weakness in its share price is notable, given that the tech giant continues to deliver exceptional performance.

    In its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year. Data center revenue alone reached $107.6 billion, up 110% from the same period a year earlier.

    These results suggest that demand for AI compute infrastructure remains remarkably strong, even as investors become more cautious about how much tech companies are spending.

    Sources indicate that and while Nvidia stock trades around 36% below its 52-week high, it has eventually recovered to its previous highs each time. In fact, similar drops in 2020 and 2025 were erased within 56 and 82 days, respectively, of their lows.

    It has been revealed that specifically, across eight recoveries from declines of at least 20%, Nvidia took a median of around 75 days from its trough to regain its previous high. But some recoveries took considerably longer, particularly following the late 2018 sell-off.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that of course, owning Nvidia stock comes with risks. For one, the company's recent leadership challenges have introduced uncertainty, while U.S. export restrictions and competition from custom AI chips could limit some of its future growth.

    Despite that, at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 10 times, Nvidia stock looks modestly priced for a company still growing revenue at triple-digit rates.

    Meanwhile, the next tech giant is focused on custom chips to drive long-term growth.

    Broadcom is benefiting from a different part of the AI infrastructure opportunity: custom-designed chips and high-speed networking. This is where the tech giant has established a strong competitive position.

    In practice, Broadcom works with hyperscalers to design custom AI chips and supplies networking hardware to connect complex infrastructure for running AI workloads. Here's how that has shown up in the numbers.

    In its third-quarter fiscal 2026 results, Broadcom reported revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year over year. More importantly, AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, representing 221% growth. Management also projected AI semiconductor revenue of $21.7 billion for the following quarter, an increase of 236% from the previous year.

    Recent findings suggest that right now, Broadcom's shares trade around 39% below their 52-week high. And like Nvidia, they've declined about as much in the past.

    Sources indicate that for example, in the 2022 bear market, Broadcom's shares declined by around 36%; by 48% during the COVID-19 crash; and by 40% during the 2025 tech sell-off. Yet the stock eventually recovered from those downturns. In fact, following its 2025 correction, Broadcom stock finished the year with a gain of about 49%.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that there are still risks to owning the stock. For one, Broadcom faces competition from other custom chip designers, while a slowdown in hyperscaler spending could affect demand for its AI products. These are reflected in the stock's forward P/E of 17 times, which also looks modest given its strong semiconductor growth and solid free cash flow (FCF).

    Nvidia and Broadcom are among the biggest companies in the AI infrastructure boom, but their recent pullbacks raise an important question: Is today's volatility a good buying opportunity?

    In a recent development, both companies have experienced painful corrections, but their underlying businesses continue to benefit from the ongoing AI build-out. Indeed, history highlights that major drawdowns don't necessarily signal the end of a company's bull case. Ultimately, if earnings continue expanding and AI spending remains strong, today's lower share prices could look like attractive entry points.

    It has been revealed that as for what comes next, Nvidia could suit value-minded investors, given its lower forward P/E. Broadcom could appeal to those seeking faster AI semiconductor growth and greater upside to analyst targets.

    By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 26, 2026 at 7:08PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dell Technologies ›.

    Though artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have taken a beating lately, the financial performance of companies in this sector remains solid.

    In a recent development, we have already seen that several AI infrastructure companies, specifically semiconductor stocks, have delivered impressive growth in revenue and earnings this earnings season. And now, Dell Technologies (DELL +0.60%), another key component of the AI data center ecosystem, has delivered phenomenal results.

    Let's take a closer look at Dell's performance and guidance and check why Wall Street is bullish about this tech stock's prospects over the coming year.

    Sources indicate that dell released its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 30) on Nov. 24. The company's revenue jumped by 103% year over year to a record $54.9 billion, well above the $49.3 billion consensus estimate. Dell's non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased at a significantly faster pace of 265% year over year to a record $9.45. Wall Street would have settled for EPS of $6.59.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The incredible demand for the tech giant's AI-optimized servers is behind this stunning performance. The company sold $22 billion worth of AI-optimized servers last quarter, up by 291% from the prior-year period. What's more, even traditional servers and networking equipment were in terrific demand, with revenue from their sales increasing by 235% year over year to $15 billion.

    What's worth noting is that Dell received way more orders than it fulfilled last quarter. Specifically, the firm booked $60.2 billion in new orders for its AI servers, taking its total AI backlog to $132.3 billion. It is worth noting that Dell received $60.9 billion in AI server orders in fiscal Q2 as well, which helps explain why its revenue pipeline continues to improve.

    Healthy demand for AI servers has prompted Dell to raise its annual guidance once again. The tech giant now expects 78% revenue growth in fiscal 2027 to $202 billion, higher than the previous estimate of $192 billion. It was originally expecting a 23% increase in revenue at the beginning of the fiscal year, to $140 billion. Even better, Dell now sees its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS jumping by 188% to $29.68, more than double its $12.90 EPS guidance at the beginning of the year.

    In a recent development, though Dell hasn't issued fiscal 2028 guidance yet, I won't be surprised if the manufacturer sustains its phenomenal momentum next year. That's because Dell already has a massive backlog, pointing to a significant increase in AI server revenue next year. The company is on track to end fiscal 2027 with $78 billion in AI revenue, more than 3x the $25 billion it generated from this segment last year.

    Dell's backlog is likely to increase again this quarter, as the firm notes that its order "pipeline grew sequentially and remains multiples of our backlog." That should set up Dell's AI server business for another year of exponential growth in fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028 and overlaps with most of calendar 2027).

    So, Dell stock seems well-placed for another impressive year in 2027 following 125% returns in 2026 as of this writing. That's exactly what Wall Street expects from the stock.

    Industry observers note that dell has a 12-month median price target of $512.50, according to estimates compiled by CNN. That's 72% higher than its current stock price.

    Recent findings suggest that it is easy to see why analysts expect such strong upside from Dell next year. The company is growing at a red-hot pace and has a price-to-earnings ratio of just 12.5, lower than the S&P 500 index's earnings multiple of 20.3. The average earnings growth of S&P 500 companies is expected to be 33% in 2026, and Dell is on track to grow at a significantly faster pace.

    Also, Dell's healthy backlog should help it outperform Wall Street's expectations again next year. It is worth noting that analysts have raised their earnings-per-share estimates for Dell following its latest report.

    DELL EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    Assuming Dell's EPS reaches $32.87 in fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028) and it trades at 20 times earnings, in line with the S&P 500's earnings multiple, the stock could jump to $657. That's 117% higher than the current stock price, suggesting that this AI stock could more than double over the next year. As such, buying Dell is a no-brainer right now considering its phenomenal growth and cheap valuation, which should set the stock up for a solid 2027.

That instantly made it one of the world's largest companies, one of the largest technology companies, and one of the biggest direct plays on artificial intelligence (AI). If you have set your sights on buying the stock, you aren't alone. But before you jump aboard, make sure you make this one portfolio move (and this one mindset move that goes with it).

    At this point, it seems like everyone agrees that artificial intelligence will change the world. So it is completely understandable that you would want to buy one of the biggest companies in the AI space after it goes public. However, you need to step back and think about the risks. And not the risks that AI may pose to humanity. The risks inherent in new technologies.

    Industry observers note that going back to the last big technology, the internet changed the world, but not every internet firm turned out to be a big winner. For example, Yahoo! was once an industry giant, but it is now just a shadow of its former self. But the fact that not all companies involved in a technological revolution survive is nothing newly introduced. There are only a handful of major automobile manufacturers around today because many more went bankrupt or got swallowed up by larger competitors. Trains went through the same cycle.

    It has been revealed that look at any technological advance, and you'll see something similar. Lots of companies rush in, but only a small number survive and thrive. Anthropic is a leader today, but it may not be one of the survivors over the long term. Which is why the one thing you need to do before buying it is make sure your portfolio is diversified. If all you own is technology stocks, even if you own 100 of them, you are not diversified.

    To be diversified, you should own stocks of as many as 50 companies across various sectors. No single investment should make up a disproportionate share of your portfolio. While there's no exact number here, 50 stocks suggests that each stock should be around 2% of your portfolio. From a sector allocation perspective, tech makes up around 37% of the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.25%), which should probably be the high end of your range.

    According to recent reports, the key is that you are trying to limit the risk that Anthropic flames out in a blaze of glory. In fact, the stock has already been highly volatile, dipping below its IPO price.

    It has been revealed that owning Anthropic is fine, but the best place for it is in a well-diversified portfolio, where the investment's inherent risks can be offset by other holdings. This brings up another vital consideration: thinking long term. Anthropic is at the forefront of AI, a new technology that is still evolving. Nobody knows what that technology will look like in a year, let alone a decade. However, that's exactly why you should go in thinking that Anthropic will be a long-term holding. Trying to time its ups and downs will be just as difficult as timing any other investment, and the failure rate is likely to be high.

    In a recent development, it is exciting to own new companies in new sectors, but it comes with risks. You have to understand those risks and make accommodations for them. Which is why the number one portfolio move here is diversification, backed by a long-term investment mentality. It is perfectly fine to buy Anthropic, but only if you go in fully understanding and preparing for the risks that it entails.

    Stocks Are Plunging Right Now. Here's What History Claims Investors Should Do.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that watching stocks plunge can make even the most seasoned investors nervous.
    • In a recent development, but now, some markets are turning lower again.
    • Perhaps the most tempting reaction during a market sell-off is to sell everything and "wait for the market to improve." The problem with the strategy is that it requires investors to get two decisions right: when to sell and when to buy back in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Orford – Nov 26, 2026 at 9:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Recent findings suggest that watching stocks plunge can make even the most seasoned investors nervous. Indeed, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.33%) closed in correction territory on Nov. 20. From there, the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -0.62%) surged 6.5%, and the S&P 500 jumped 4.7% on Nov. 23.

    In a recent development, but now, some markets are turning lower again. So, before rushing to sell, it's worth looking at what history tells us about market downturns and why staying invested may be the smarter move.

    Perhaps the most tempting reaction during a market sell-off is to sell everything and "wait for the market to improve." The problem with the strategy is that it requires investors to get two decisions right: when to sell and when to buy back in.

    In fact, seven of the market's 10 best trading days over 20 years occurred within 15 days of its 10 worst days. As a result, investors who sell during periods of extreme volatility risk realizing temporary losses, while missing out on the recovery.

    The latest bout of volatility is a good example.

    Tech stocks were hit hard in November as investors questioned whether the enormous investments in artificial intelligence would ever generate strong returns. Indeed, concerns about semiconductor demand, regulatory complications, and a possible slowdown in AI spending added to the pressure.

    Recent findings suggest that these developments are certainly worth watching, but the broader U.S. market has repeatedly shown its ability to recover and reach latest highs over time.

    Sources indicate that of course, staying invested doesn't mean blindly holding just any stock regardless of what's happening in the markets. Broad sell-offs can create buying opportunities, but investors need to distinguish between quality companies whose stocks are "cheap" and businesses that are fundamentally weakening.

    Recent findings suggest that for example, the recent concerns surrounding AI are worth considering. Investors have become more sensitive to the enormous capital expenditures (capex) required to build data centers, develop advanced chips, and expand compute infrastructure. Plus, questions about monetization, financing, and competition have contributed to volatility across the tech sector.

    According to recent reports, to be fair, these are real concerns. Not every AI company will become a long-term winner, and some of today's valuations have become difficult to justify. However, that doesn't necessarily invalidate the broader AI investment opportunity.

    Specifically, companies with durable competitive advantages, strong balance sheets, recurring revenue, and credible paths to profitability may still be well positioned to benefit from AI adoption.

    Beyond individual stocks, investors can also look at how balanced their overall portfolios are.

    A steep correction can expose just how much risk an investor has in a particular industry, tech giant, or asset class. That's why diversification and rebalancing matter a lot.

    To start, investors can review whether their current portfolios still align with their financial goals, time horizon, and risk tolerance. For example, someone who has become overly concentrated in high-growth tech stocks may want to diversify into other, less-correlated sectors. On top of that, holding a broader mix of businesses across industries, alongside assets like bonds and cash, can help reduce dependence on any single market theme.

    Rebalancing can also have an opposite effect. In practice, when stocks fall, their weighting in a portfolio may decline. Investors with enough liquidity could consider gradually adding to certain asset classes and bringing their allocations closer to their original targets.

    Ultimately, staying disciplined and avoiding emotional decisions can help investors weather volatility and stay focused on the long term.

    History has shown that panic selling can be costly, especially as investors risk missing out on the eventual recovery. Instead of trying to time the market, investors can focus on what they can control. This could mean maintaining a diversified portfolio, investing consistently, and revisiting their holdings.

    It has been revealed that after all, during corrections, patience and discipline may actually be more valuable than trying to predict what happens next. In the end, staying invested may simply be the best move for long-term investors.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    The Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) fallout has truly been incredible. At its peak, Nvidia's market cap was nearly $5.8 trillion. Now, it's about $3.6 trillion. That's more than $2 trillion in losses, and only five companies in the world have a market cap greater than that. That's hard to wrap your mind around, but Nvidia's loss of value since CEO Jensen Huang resigned and returned is unparalleled.

    Nvidia is now down around 35% from its all-time high. That's significant because it is now tied for the deepest sell-off Nvidia has faced since the AI build-out kicked off in 2023. The previous deepest sell-off occurred in April 2025 when tariff fears drove the stock market down. However, that peaked at about a 35% sell-off.

    It has been revealed that with Nvidia at its cheapest point in a long time, is it worth buying? Or do investors have more to worry about? Let's take a look.

    In a recent development, even before Huang resigned as CEO, there was trouble with Nvidia's stock. The market was a bit concerned about industry-wide AI spending and assumed it could not last forever, so it discounted Nvidia's stock. The idea here was that AI spending would decrease, harming Nvidia. However, that is looking like a bad assumption.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    During the manufacturer's Q3 earnings call, interim CEO and current CFO Colette Kress increased revenue growth guidance for next year from 70% to 75%. That is due to extreme demand for AI from hyperscalers and won't change regardless of who leads Nvidia.

    That is great news for shareholders, and if that growth comes to fruition, there's no way that Nvidia will stay at its current level.

    The reality is that Huang built Nvidia into such a giant and dominant organization that it can run itself for a few years. While there were concerns about what the future of Nvidia looks like without him, those fears are now gone with him back in the CEO role. Still, Huang must testify before Congress to address some of the events that happened as CEO and explain what controls they have on chips or trade secrets that shouldn't have fallen into China's hands, but might have. Huang and Nvidia have a ways to go before they're in the clear, but Nvidia's expected growth isn’t changing.

    But where will next year's growth take it?

    For this fiscal year, Wall Street analysts estimate its revenue will total $424 billion. If Nvidia hits that figure (the firm has a strong track record of exceeding estimates) and grows by 75% next year, that would put its revenue at $742 billion. One of Nvidia's impressive characteristics is its profit margin, which has sat at 62% over the past 12 months. If the company can maintain that level, it would generate $460 billion in profits. That's right, Nvidia's profits should be larger next year than its revenue is this year.

    Sources indicate that that's a simply incredible projection, and given how aggressive the AI hyperscalers are about scaling up computing power, I think it's realistic. With that money, Nvidia could do all sorts of things, including repurchasing a large amount of outstanding shares. This may be a viable option because Nvidia's stock is cheap right now, trading for a mere 9 times next year's earnings estimates.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    Few stocks in the market trade at that level and are growing at a market-beating pace, let alone one that is expected to grow at a 75% pace next year.

    Nvidia is one of the greatest values on the stock market right now; I think it's a no-brainer buy, and investors should be scooping up shares while they are massively discounted.

    Sources indicate that space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%) could lend a hand, but it probably won't. Which is why more aggressive investors might find SpaceX of interest. Here's what you need to know.

    Industry observers note that spaceX is at the front of the pack in the space race. And it really is a race, as companies attempt to stake out their position in the still-emerging space industry. Amazon has basically made a huge bet with SpaceX competitor ULA, which is presently looking less desirable. The cost of losing the 40 satellites is bad enough, but it isn't the end of the issue. Amazon will need to build 40 more to replace them, and then get those satellites into space. But ULA's setback is likely to lead to delays on that front, as it works out what happened. This could complicate ULA's plans to increase its launch cadence.

    This is good news for SpaceX because Amazon is attempting to create a satellite system to compete with SpaceX's Starlink. But there's more to the story here. SpaceX has been highly successful in its releases, sending many spacecraft into orbit. It could offer its services to other companies, including Amazon. To be fair, it does. But it looks like SpaceX is increasingly using its launches to orbit its own satellites.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Basically, SpaceX holds a leading position in both its Starlink service and its launch services. Other companies are playing catch-up, and that's not working out particularly well. Thus, SpaceX's lead is maintained, if not extended, in both niches of the industry with each successful launch. This is an industrial giant that is flexing its muscles.

    But it is hard to value SpaceX as a business. For starters, it has only been public for a short while, so there's not much history to go on. But even if you take the strong third-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 161% and the company's positive earnings of $0.35 per share into account, you can't ignore the massive capital spending that's going on. Or the massive capital spending that is likely to be needed in the future.

    To put a number on that spending, SpaceX spent $19.6 billion on capital investments in the third quarter alone. Roughly $1.6 billion of that went to its space operations, $1.5 billion to connectivity, and a shockingly large $16.6 billion to the manufacturer's artificial intelligence division. None of that spending was optional, and there's likely to be plenty more capital investment to follow in the years ahead.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that and while SpaceX reported positive earnings in the third quarter, its year-to-date total through the first three quarters of 2026 remains negative. In other words, SpaceX is a money-losing business spending huge sums to grow. That's a high-risk proposition that only the most aggressive investors should be considering.

    If you are going to buy SpaceX, you have to believe that the tech giant will remain an industry leader. This is the kind of company you buy and hold for the long term. So far, at least in the space and satellite connectivity sectors, it remains top of class, with little indication of that changing anytime soon given the failed ULA launch.

    Recent findings suggest that notably, Wall Street is generally positive about the future, assigning SpaceX an average target price of $256 per share, well above the $127 per share as of this writing. However, volatility is likely to be extreme, as it has already been even over the stock's short trading history. If you can't handle that, you shouldn't own the stock.

    Jerry Jones still confident about Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer, doesn't expect coaching change after Thanksgiving loss to Eagles

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanksgiving wound up being a very bad night for Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, but it apparently won't cost him his job.
    • Industry observers note that immediately after the Cowboys' collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday, team owner Jerry Jones told reporters he doesn't expect to make a coaching change any time soon.
    • "I wouldn't anticipate that, no, at this juncture.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanksgiving wound up being a very bad night for Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, but it apparently won't cost him his job.

    Industry observers note that immediately after the Cowboys' collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday, team owner Jerry Jones told reporters he doesn't expect to make a coaching change any time soon. Instead, Jones suggested continuity would give Dallas its best chance in the coming weeks.

    Via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram:.

    "I wouldn't anticipate that, no, at this juncture. We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes.".

    The Cowboys face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 13, then have a bye before facing the Los Angeles Rams on Dec. 20.

    Jones went on to say he was still "confident" about Schottenheimer, but made clear that confidence was based on nothing the team indicated Thursday:.

    "Nothing we've seen out here tonight, but you've got to look at everything. That's certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time. We've got several more games to go and we've got to have our mind on that.".

    Thanksgiving really was that bad for the Cowboys, who led 28-10 at halftime and held a lead as large as 21 points near the end of the third quarter.

    Brian Schottenheimer had a bad Thanksgiving.

    Sources indicate that the team was then hit with a cascading series of disasters. Former Cowboys backup Joe Milton led the Eagles to touchdowns on three of their next four drives, with the Eagles also returning a blocked punt for a touchdown. The Cowboys still had the advantage in the final minute, but decided to go for it on fourth down in Eagles territory and watched Dak Prescott get sacked.

    Eagles kicker Jake Elliott proceeded to make a 59-yard field goal in the final seconds. A Prescott interception ended the game.

    Industry observers note that both the overall collapse and late-game decision-making left nearly every finger in Dallas pointing at Schottenheimer, who has been facing the hot seat for some time. He mentioned he wasn't worried about such speculation after the game, via Jon Machota of The Athletic:.

    It has been revealed that "I don't worry about that. I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn't affect me.".

    Recent findings suggest that schottenheimer's hire was controversial when it was first unveiled, as he was hardly a popular offensive coordinator under previous head coach Mike McCarthy (who is dealing with issues of his own right now). Jones' decision to promote Schottenheimer demanded trust in his own team's operations, and the results have been a 12-16-1 record.

    In more than three decades of owning the Cowboys, Jones has fired only a single head coach during the season: Wade Phillips in 2010. Jones has said he regrets that decision and that could very well be informing his thinking here, though that will hardly protect Schottenheimer in a month and a half.

    Industry observers note that the recent sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks triggered a correction in the stock market. The S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.25%) fell by more than 10% from its recent highs and is struggling to remain in positive territory for the year.

    During times like these, it's easy for investors to worry that they're picking the wrong stocks. Or worry that the stock market is a bad place to put their money -- what if the S&P 500 goes down by another 10% next month?

    If you want to invest in the stock market, times like these are actually some of the best moments to put money to work, because many stocks are trading at lower prices than just a few weeks ago.

    Recent findings suggest that and you don't have to pick stocks to make great money in the stock market. Just buying a low-cost index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -0.28%) can deliver life-changing returns in the long run.

    Let's look at just how much you could make from steady $200 monthly investments in VOO.

    In a recent development, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) is one of the most popular ways to invest in the stock market because it charges ultra-low fees (0.03% expense ratio) and it holds 500 of the largest, most crucial publicly traded stocks in America. When you buy VOO, you're getting the entire S&P 500 index: 500 of the most profitable large-cap stocks. When America's largest publicly traded companies do well, so will you.

    Industry observers note that this index changes day by day as some stocks go up and others go down, weighted by market cap. For example, if one manufacturer has a bad month, the S&P 500 index will hold a slightly lower amount of its stock than it did a month ago. If another company performs better, its stock will account for a larger percentage of the S&P 500 by weight.

    In a recent development, this means that the S&P 500 index is constantly sorting the "winners" and "losers" for you. This doesn't mean that the S&P 500 index always goes up or is guaranteed to deliver positive returns. But because S&P 500 ETFs like VOO hold 500 stocks, they are broadly diversified. That tends to make their performance less volatile over the long run than that of individual stocks or sector-specific ETFs.

    In the past five years, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF has delivered annualized returns of about 12%.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    But if you're worried that the recent stock market correction will mean lower returns in the future, keep this in mind: over the long run, since 1928, the S&P 500 has delivered annualized returns of 9.98%. That's lower than the past five years, but still a strong return.

    Recent findings suggest that let's assume that VOO can continue delivering 9.98% annualized returns over the coming years -- even if there are bear markets along the way. And let's assume that someone starts investing $200 a month at age 30 and keeps investing for 37 years until their Social Security retirement age of 67.

    If you invested $200 per month in VOO and earned 9.98% average annual return of 9.98%, after 10 years, your investments would grow to $38,213. After 20 years, you'd have $137,148. After 30 years, you'd have $393,294. And after 37 years, your investments would be worth $788,199.

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 27, 2026 at 2:03AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Industry observers note that anthropic’s (ANT +1.08%) first two days as a publicly traded organization were already days for the history books. It started off trading at about $110 per share before closing at $97. That's still a double-digit percentage gain from its list price, so it was a great day. Then it was caught up in a rout of AI stocks and, on Nov. 24, fell below its IPO price.

    Recent findings suggest that with a tumultuous start, Anthropic is an intriguing stock, but is it a buy? Here's where I think Anthropic could end the year priced, and investors may want to pay attention to get maximum returns.

    Recent findings suggest that there are multiple ways to engage in the AI investing trend. You could invest in a hardware supplier like Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) or Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%), or in a utility manufacturer benefiting from increased electricity usage. There are also construction companies and AI hyperscalers that are putting up hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of data center infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, however, all these styles of investments have one thing in common: None of them are 100% pure-play AI investments. These companies all have other business units that aren't exposed to AI. There are very few AI-focused stocks on the market, as the entry costs to get into the AI game are quite high.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    However, all that changed when Anthropic went public. Anthropic is one of the two primary AI labs (the other being OpenAI). So, with it going public first, it is drawing a lot of investor interest. Anthropic is the poster child for AI investing, as all of its business comes from the usage of its Claude family of AI models. The more AI is used, the better Anthropic does. So, if the market is bullish on AI, Anthropic will do great. If it's bearish, the market will suffer.

    In a recent development, right now, it's pretty clear that the market has an overall bearish stance on the AI build-out. However, that's mostly the market making its opinion on massive infrastructure spending known. There isn't much that will stop the AI hyperscalers from investing in data centers, as they see a massive opportunity.

    Sources indicate that anthropic is a bit different from most AI companies, as it doesn't own any computing assets. Instead, it chooses to rent them. So, the risk exposure from overbuilding is practically nothing, since it only rents computing power rather than owning it. That should help it be analyzed from a pure AI usage standpoint by the market, but if market sentiment is going one way, nothing will be able to save Anthropic from further downturn.

    So, what's in store for the rest of 2026?

    The reality is that the AI sector is being harmed by one company: Nvidia. The resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have shaken the AI industry, but aside from Nvidia, there really aren't many domino effects. Anthropic will be just fine.

    It has been revealed that I think the market will come to this realization over the next few weeks, and Anthropic stock will be bought up in December so that portfolio managers can show their clients they bought the hot fresh AI stock. This could contribute to Anthropic rising in a Santa Claus rally – the name of the rally that occurs during December due to heavy buying.

    According to recent reports, as a result, I wouldn't be surprised if Anthropic's stock returned to the $ 110-per-share level it opened at on Nov. 19.

    It has been revealed that on the flip side, if the market indicates bearish on AI, there could be more downside from here. However, I think the odds of that are lower, so I'm confident in saying Anthropic has ample upside from here.

    Major chipmakers and operating systems are building hardware support for Versatile Video Coding, or VVC, an advanced video compression standard. InterDigital holds foundational patents in VVC, allowing it to collect incremental royalties as video streaming adoption grows across mobile devices and platforms.

    Recent findings suggest that european courts issued multiple injunctions against The Walt Disney Firm over video encoding and casting patents, finding that Disney acted as an unwilling licensee. Legal victories validate the strength of the patent portfolio and push reluctant media companies toward binding arbitration or settled commercial terms.

    Revenue from existing contracts is tracking ahead of full-year expectations, and management isn't hiding its satisfaction with operational execution.

    According to recent reports, predictable recurring revenues, low capital intensity, and an internal research engine that produces six fresh patents daily position the business to generate steady free cash flow. Management is watching capital returns, legal enforcement outcomes, and hardware adoption of new video codecs. Long-term fixed-fee contracts protect profit margins and support ongoing research investments alongside share buybacks and dividend payments.

    Cowboys owner Jerry Jones offered strong praise for Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Dallas' late loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving.

    McCarthy, who coached the Cowboys from 2020 to 2024, has been in the headlines this week after his former quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, leveled a series of accusations against him Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    It has been revealed that rodgers remarked McCarthy slept during meetings, didn't watch film and even used the wrong team name while breaking a huddle. Since that interview aired, local beat reporters have cited anonymous sources in the building who confirmed some of the claims.

    While the timing likely could have been better, Jones still took the time to address the claims, and he ended up giving McCarthy his full support with effusive praise.

    In a recent development, "I offered him [McCarthy] to stay at least another year when he left. I thought he was outstanding as the head coach. Had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him.

    Industry observers note that he's, frankly, one of the finest people around football that I've been around. I can't say enough about him.

    I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract, any of that it was never on the table. We never had an issue within the organization.".

    After the 2024 season, the two sides reportedly reached an impasse in contract talks and mutually agreed to part ways.

    McCarthy ended his tenure in Dallas with a 49-35 record.

    According to recent reports, jones is the latest to defend McCarthy this week. Ahead of each Thanksgiving Day game, hosts on pregame shows defended the head coach and criticized how Rodgers delivered his message.

    Former Steelers quarterbacks Terry Bradshaw and Russell Wilson, as well as Hall of Famer Michael Strahan, were among those who spoke out against Rodgers' public delivery of criticism of McCarthy.

    #142441. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (742 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the manufacturer to fulfill all of its previously revealed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider mentioned in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Sources indicate that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Sources indicate that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    In a recent development, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    It has been revealed that coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, noted CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    Industry observers note that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my tech giant every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real glitch is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    #142428. Breaking: Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Recent findings suggest that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • In a recent development, first, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Recent findings suggest that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    In a recent development, first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout swiftly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    Recent findings suggest that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    According to recent reports, the major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #142417. Tech Report: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (634 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • It has been revealed that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Industry observers note that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession strategy, makes it worse.

    It has been revealed that however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Industry observers note that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    It has been revealed that this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    Industry News: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at fresh highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at fresh highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the manufacturer's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the manufacturer as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Recent findings suggest that barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks newly introduced CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to swiftly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the organization's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway claims it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most notable ideas.

    WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    In a recent development, two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    Industry observers note that and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that indicates it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

Currently, 14% of the fund's assets are tied to Anthropic, according to the tech giant's website.Options volume on the fund jumped to more than 10x the 30-day average Monday, according to Cboe LiveVol data. Of the 42,300 contracts traded by midday, 41,800 were calls, with just 141 puts likely opened by buyers.

    Industry observers note that just shy of $5.5 million in options premium on DXYZ traded on Monday, with almost all of it tied to calls, but just marginally more spent buying than selling calls, according to SpotGamma. The highest-volume contract is currently the 30-strike call expiring Friday, a 90-cent contract that needs the fund to rally 19% into the weekend to pay off.Traders may want to be wary of how the fund traded around the SpaceX IPO: DXYZ surged almost 150% in May before unwinding all the gains in the weeks ahead of SpaceX's debut. Since then, the fund has barely moved, trading around $26.There are other bullish signs surrounding Anthropic's IPO in the derivatives markets. Current prices for perpetual futures on the blockchain exchange Hyperliquid are implying an opening price of $98, a substantial pop from the $70-$78 price range quoted in the company's amended S1 filing. The AI giant is expected to price Wednesday evening and begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

    #142383. S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (471 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (471 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the company continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings mentioned in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
    • "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P remarked in a Wednesday note.
    • Nvidia presently holds an AA rating, the third-highest level.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the company continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings mentioned in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.

    "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P remarked in a Wednesday note.

    Nvidia presently holds an AA rating, the third-highest level.

    S&P has placed the chipmaker on "CreditWatch with negative implications," though any potential downgrade would be limited to one notch, to AA-, unless investigations or disclosures lead the agency to conclude that Nvidia's reputation or future prospects have also been harmed.

    A downgrade can pressure bond prices, push yields higher and raise borrowing costs. Nvidia priced $25 billion of investment-grade senior notes in June, with maturities from 2028 through 2056, shortly after S&P upgraded the manufacturer from AA- to AA.

    Nvidia has about $32.5 billion of bonds in the U.S. high-grade corporate bond index, according to Bloomberg.

    In a recent development, S&P's Wednesday note follows Moody's Ratings changing its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive on Nov. 18, citing governance concerns, and leaving that outlook unchanged after Huang's return on Monday.

    In its note, S&P cited the "long tenure" of certain board members as a reason their independence may be "compromised" and said Nvidia's management and governance risk was "rising.".

    The ratings agency added that it remained unaware of any remedial action taken by the board to address what could be "meaningful" management and governance deficiencies.

    In a recent development, chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have served on Nvidia's board since 1993, while Brooke Seawell joined in 1997. Mark Stevens served from 1993 to 2006 and rejoined the board in 2008.

    S&P also flagged questions around geopolitical risk management and internal controls arising from Nvidia's exposure to China.

    "While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the "key man" risk to the forefront," S&P's Andrew Chang and David Tsui noted.

    Chang and Tsui noted that Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement did not resolve questions about the board's oversight of executive conduct.

    The agency also intends to meet with Nvidia's board and management to discuss plans to address those deficiencies, particularly around "board independence, effective management oversight and a credible leadership succession initiative.".

    Huang returned less than two weeks after Jones said Nvidia's directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back, sending Nvidia shares up as much as 36% during Monday's session.

    Nvidia shares are down about 12.5% since Monday's close.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy situation in Pittsburgh: 'It's a dumpster fire'

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin discussed with NBC's Mike Tirico his reaction to everything Aaron Rodgers stated in a scathing critique during Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".
    • The highlight of the interview was Tomlin's response when asked about his emotions watching what is happening with the Steelers after coaching the team for two decades.
    • It's a dumpster fire and I don't say that in a judgmental way.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin discussed with NBC's Mike Tirico his reaction to everything Aaron Rodgers stated in a scathing critique during Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    The highlight of the interview was Tomlin's response when asked about his emotions watching what is happening with the Steelers after coaching the team for two decades.

    "I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire and I don't say that in a judgmental way. I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset.".

    Tomlin started the interview by being asked for his general reaction to what was stated.

    "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday. The prevailing one is general sadness.

    "Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rogers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.".

    The former Steelers head coach noted he was "shocked" at how the team's dirty laundry was aired.

    " … I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed against Mike [McCarthy] and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time.".

    Tomlin was asked his opinion on whether or not this will negatively impact McCarthy's ability to lead the Steelers.

    "It certainly created some challenges and challenges is an understatement if those things are true. But his ability or inability to overcome that is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys buy into what he's selling. Certainly he's been there a short period of time so certainly you wonder the level of that challenge. Certainly it is relationship-based.".

    On Tuesday night after 11 ET, it was announced that Rodgers would be inactive for the Steelers' Friday game against the Denver Broncos, and that Mason Rudolph would start.

    The next day, Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on McCarthy, accusing him of sleeping during meetings, not watching film, and using the wrong team name during a breakdown of a team huddle.

    The rant sent the football world into a frenzy as local reporters confirmed anonymous sources saying it was all true, and former players and coaches, current analysts, NFL insiders and a team owner came out in support of McCarthy.

    Tomlin was the head coach of the Steelers from 2007 to 2025. He famously never had a losing season, but also hadn't made the Super Bowl since the 2008 season.

    At the end of the 2025 season, Rodgers' first year with the franchise, Tomlin resigned, triggering a coaching search that ended with McCarthy's hiring.
