    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Industry observers note that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting major moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Industry observers note that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the manufacturer that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the organization's after-market report on Tuesday.

    According to recent reports, since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    Industry observers note that one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    Recent findings suggest that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Wealthy Europeans look beyond stocks amid AI selloff. Here’s where they’re investing

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Wealthy Europeans are looking to alternative asset classes to build exposure to artificial intelligence themes amid turbulence in public markets.
    • Goldman Sachs Alternatives' inaugural survey of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors found 47% of European respondents saw alternatives as the best way to gain exposure to AI and future tech growth, compared to just 24% of U.S.
    • The survey found a significant gap between the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Wealthy Europeans are looking to alternative asset classes to build exposure to artificial intelligence themes amid turbulence in public markets.

    Goldman Sachs Alternatives' inaugural survey of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors found 47% of European respondents saw alternatives as the best way to gain exposure to AI and future tech growth, compared to just 24% of U.S. investors.

    The survey found a significant gap between the U.S. and Europe in terms of investor knowledge of alternatives, which include assets like private equity, property and infrastructure. Goldman said 82% of European respondents are familiar with the alternative investments market — compared to 50% of U.S. investors.

    It has been revealed that goldman polled 1,000 investors with at least 1 million in investable assets in their local currency across the U.K., France, Germany, Italy and Switzerland. The survey was carried out between June 29 and Aug. 18 this year.

    The report on the findings, published Wednesday, did not specify the proportion of respondents who already have a stake in some kind of alternative investment — but wealthy Europeans appeared particularly bullish on the space.

    Recent findings suggest that private equity made up the largest proportion of current alternatives holdings. Among wealthy Europeans with alternatives exposure, 62% said they invested in private equity. The second most commonly held asset class was private real estate, which was backed by 51% of European alternatives investors. Hedge funds were held by 37% of European alternatives owners, and private infrastructure was held by 30%.

    One in four respondents who did not already own an alternative investment mentioned they were likely to invest in the market in the coming 12 months. Among those already in the space, 26% said they were likely to increase their allocations over the next year, while just 5% said they planned to decrease their exposure.

    Sources indicate that of the European investors who already owned alternatives, 54% mentioned their assets had performed as expected, while 44% said their assets had exceeded their expectations to the upside. Only 2% said their alternative investments had performed worse than expected.

    "Recent reforms gave individual investors unprecedented access to alternative asset classes like private equity, venture capital, and private credit," Kyle Kniffen, global head of alternatives for third-party wealth at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, said in Wednesday's report.

    He added that wealthy investors "look ready to jump at the opportunity.".

    "Our survey reveals satisfaction among current alts owners is high and adoption looks set to increase," Kniffen noted.

    Alternative investments have increasingly become a staple of high-net-worth individuals' investment portfolios.

    Over the past year, JPMorgan Asset Management's private wealth alternative assets in the Asia-Pacific region have jumped 40%, while BNY Wealth says alternative investments now account for 60% of single-family office portfolios — recently surpassing traditional assets for the first time.

    According to recent reports, but investing in alternatives carries risks. Private equity, for example, can lock up capital for long periods, and although the number of exits ticked slightly higher last year, the value of those deals fell.

    Concerns about private credit, meanwhile, have dominated headlines, with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warning on Oct. 14, 2025, that "cockroaches" were likely to be lurking in private markets.

    — CNBC's Lee Ying Shan contributed to this article.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘Ready for any storm’: UAE minister optimistic on economy as IMF lifts forecast

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (365 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The UAE is "very optimistic" about achieving 7%-8% growth next year, the country's economy and tourism minister Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri told CNBC after the latest data from the International Monetary Fund highlighted the country would avoid a recession in 2026.
    • The IMF last week revised the UAE's real GDP forecast to 0.2% growth in 2026 from a 3.9% contraction predicted a month ago.
    • He said the tourism industry was already picking up with occupancy rates returning to "almost near normal" and international carriers including British Airways and Air France rerouting flights to the UAE.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The UAE is "very optimistic" about achieving 7%-8% growth next year, the country's economy and tourism minister Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri told CNBC after the latest data from the International Monetary Fund highlighted the country would avoid a recession in 2026.

    The IMF last week revised the UAE's real GDP forecast to 0.2% growth in 2026 from a 3.9% contraction predicted a month ago. "The UAE is coming back, and that adjustment within one month shows that there is a huge potential aspect when it comes towards the end of the year," the minister told CNBC's Dan Murphy.

    He said the tourism industry was already picking up with occupancy rates returning to "almost near normal" and international carriers including British Airways and Air France rerouting flights to the UAE. The minister expects economic growth to be higher than 0.2% this year.

    The Iran war has disrupted economic activity in the UAE, with missile and drone attacks from Tehran and maritime disruptions weighing on energy trade, tourism, aviation and private-sector confidence.

    Earlier this month, U.S. President Donald Trump mentioned that renewed attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" if negotiations produce a "very strong agreement." However, on Monday, Trump threatened that Tehran could face fresh U.S. strikes next year if the two countries failed to strike a deal, as per Fox News.

    "We can we cannot promise the world for any storms that will land on our shore, but we can always promise that the UAE's economy is ready for any storm," Al Marri said.

    He added that next year the UAE's economy will have a "different" model than the one before the conflict and investments will be focused on building factories and "things that we really need in times of crisis.".

    The World Bank in October said it expects the UAE's economy to recover next year, driven by rising oil production and exports and a rebound in tourism, trade, transportation, financial services, and construction.

    It warned that the improvement in economic activity in the UAE largely depends on the duration and intensity of the Iran war, with a faster de-escalation likely to accelerate the recovery in services exports and private-sector activity.

    • The report claims that "after the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson mentioned in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Recent findings suggest that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the manufacturer's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Norse Atlantic suspends all flights, warns it may file for bankruptcy after share price collapse

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Norse Atlantic suspended all of its flights on Thursday and warned it may have to file for bankruptcy after its stock collapsed on Wednesday following its warning about its "critical" financial situation.
    • Oslo-listed shares of Norse closed 85% lower on Wednesday.
    • Recent findings suggest that "The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing," Norse said in a Thursday statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Norse Atlantic suspended all of its flights on Thursday and warned it may have to file for bankruptcy after its stock collapsed on Wednesday following its warning about its "critical" financial situation.

    Oslo-listed shares of Norse closed 85% lower on Wednesday.

    Recent findings suggest that "The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing," Norse said in a Thursday statement. "If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the board's intention to file for bankruptcy.".

    The airline added that "there can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found.".

    Checks by CNBC showed the airline was still selling tickets for flights on Friday and beyond as of 9 a.m. Oslo time on Thursday.

    Warning signs first popped up when PK786 from London to Islamabad and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore were cancelled because of "an unexpected operational suspension," the Pakistani flag carrier mentioned on X.

    According to recent reports, the airline had been set to operate two Pakistan International Airlines flights Wednesday under a wet-lease agreement, in which one airline provides the aircraft and crew to another. The agreement had only been signed in early October.

    PIA remarked it would operate the routes using its own Boeing 777 aircraft from the next day.

    According to recent reports, norse's own flight Z0 783 from London Gatwick to Orlando was also shown as canceled Wednesday on live air traffic website Flightradar24. London Gatwick's website listed the flight's status for Thursday as "enquire airline.".

    In a bid to stave off financial troubles, Norse cut 75 jobs in May as part of an effort to reduce costs by $50 million, after Eivind Roald replaced founder Bjorn Tore Larsen as CEO in November last year.

    The Norwegian carrier said Wednesday that its situation depended on securing financing for short-term liquidity needs and that it was in discussions about a potential strategic takeover.

    "Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution," the airline mentioned.

    The Norwegian carrier has come under strain due to soaring jet fuel costs since the onset of the Iran war.

    India's largest airline, low-cost carrier IndiGo, entered an agreement with Norse Atlantic in early 2025 to lease six 787-9 aircraft as it launched flights to Europe and Britain ahead of the arrival of its own widebody planes.

    The agreement concluded at the end of October this year, with IndiGo citing airspace constraints, elevated fuel costs and currency pressures.

    According to recent reports, at its peak in 2024, Norse Atlantic had 4,822 scheduled flights. That number dipped to 4,695 in 2025 and 2,565 in 2026, according to aviation analytics company Cirium. The airline had 122 flights scheduled for November this year.

    It has been revealed that norse Atlantic CEO Roald told CNBC in May that he was not "overly concerned" about access to fuel and noted the airline had no indication at the time that the crisis would have an immediate impact. The airline said in October that it was continuing to operate at reduced capacity because of "prolonged high fuel prices.".

    Correction: This story was updated to reflect that Norse shares closed 85% lower on Wednesday.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night.

    Sources indicate that shooting guard Jaylen Brown has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games.

    Sources indicate that brown picked up the hamstring matter in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return.     With no Embiid and no Brown for a half, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey took over and led the 76ers to a win over the Heat on Wednesday. James logged his first triple-double as a 76er with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Maxey added 30 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists.

    Recent findings suggest that the win moved Philadelphia to 15-4. Friday's game against Indiana is the front end of a back-to-back, and a win would help the 76ers clinch their NBA Cup group.

    Tom Brady doesn't approve of Aaron Rodgers' comments on Mike McCarthy: 'Nobody wins when the family feuds'

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aaron Rodgers ended his Pittsburgh Steelers career in a way that will be remembered long after his time as a player ends.
    • The former Upcoming England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star and current Fox Sports broadcaster weighed in on Rodgers going scorched-earth against Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during the Philadelphia Eagles-Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving game on Thursday, suggesting Rodgers should have taken a more graceful route out of Pittsburgh:.
    • In a recent development, "The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aaron Rodgers ended his Pittsburgh Steelers career in a way that will be remembered long after his time as a player ends. Tom Brady does not appear to approve.

    The former Upcoming England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star and current Fox Sports broadcaster weighed in on Rodgers going scorched-earth against Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during the Philadelphia Eagles-Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving game on Thursday, suggesting Rodgers should have taken a more graceful route out of Pittsburgh:.

    In a recent development, "The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place. We shouldn't ever lose track of that as players. It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. Shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say.".

    The trouble for the Steelers began late Tuesday night, when the team unveiled it was benching Rodgers and starting backup quarterback Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos on Thursday. Rodgers responded by going onto his friend Pat McAfee's show and unleashing a torrent of claims about McCarthy's aptitude for the job.

    The Steelers officially released Rodgers soon after the interview. Subsequent reports indicated Rodgers demanded the team either give him play-calling duties or release him, with McCarthy later confirming Rodgers "made an ultimatum.".

    Brady praised Rodgers' career, but again indicated there wasn't much to be proud about this week:.

    Industry observers note that "Certainly a Hall of Fame career and he's a tremendous player and it has nothing to do with his play-style. I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what your team was trying to accomplish. That supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote.

    In a recent development, "Again, I was very fortunate. It was a great locker room. I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches. Nobody wins when the family feuds.".

    According to recent reports, aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady both had tension with a longtime head coach. The two situations ended very differently.

    For his part, Brady played under a grand total of three head coaches during his NFL career: Bill Belichick with the Latest England Patriots and Bruce Arians and Todd Bowles with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

    Industry observers note that perhaps reinforcing his point, it's well-known that Brady and Belichick had their friction while working together. Brady acknowledged last year that "a natural tension" developed and only ended when he left Latest England, but there was no public blow-up and Brady has otherwise supported and defended the coach since their split.

    According to recent reports, rodgers' time with McCarthy goes back to his sophomore year in the NFL in 2006, two years before his first career start. McCarthy's hire in Pittsburgh reportedly wasn't intended as a way to lure back Rodgers for another year, but it felt like a natural reunion for a pairing that once won a Super Bowl together.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia — and Denny's has a booth waiting for him.

    The American diner chain welcomed the billionaire's return as Nvidia CEO by revealing that it had reinstated a commemorative plaque marking the birthplace of the artificial intelligence chip giant after learning of its removal on Nov. 13.

    "Some things you just don't take off the menu. Jensen Huang is one of them," Denny's noted in a post on X.

    The plaque marks the booth at a Denny's restaurant in Silicon Valley, California, where Huang and his co-founders discussed the idea for Nvidia, which was founded in 1993.

    According to recent reports, the restaurant chain noted it learned on Nov. 13, a day after Huang's resignation, that the plaque had been removed.

    "We put the plaque right back up where it belongs," Denny's said, without specifying who had removed it or why.

    Huang's ties to the diner chain, however, stretch back well before Nvidia's founding. He worked at Denny's as a teenager, washing dishes and serving customers before going on to build one of the world's most valuable companies.

    In a recent development, the restaurant chain also disclosed that it had contacted Nvidia's communications team on Nov. 10 to express its pride in their shared history.

    Huang's return came less than two weeks after his sudden resignation rattled investors and raised questions about corporate governance and succession planning at the chipmaker.

    While his return has put those concerns in the spotlight, Denny's offered a simpler message to its former employee.

    "Jensen, your booth is waiting and the coffee's on. We're always open, 24/7," the restaurant chain said.

    #142346. Industry News: Eagles, ex-Cowboys QB Joe Milton III overcome 21-point deficit to stun Dallas: 'I know that defense like the back of my hand'

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1883 w)

    Industry News: Eagles, ex-Cowboys QB Joe Milton III overcome 21-point deficit to stun Dallas: 'I know that defense like the back of my hand'

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving, kicking a 59-yard game-winning field goal with two seconds left to clinch a 39-38 victory for their second consecutive win in a crucial divisional matchup.
    • The 21-point comeback marked the largest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history.
    • It looked like the Eagles were done for, unable to muster much offense and unable to stop the Cowboys' offense.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving, kicking a 59-yard game-winning field goal with two seconds left to clinch a 39-38 victory for their second consecutive win in a crucial divisional matchup.

    The 21-point comeback marked the largest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history.

    It looked like the Eagles were done for, unable to muster much offense and unable to stop the Cowboys' offense. Dallas led 31-10 with 15 seconds left in the third quarter, but Philadelphia stormed back thanks to quarterback Joe Milton III's arm.

    The momentum swung in a substantial way when Milton debuted a 45-yard touchdown pass near the goal line, finding DeVonta Smith for the score.

    That was the duo's second long touchdown of the game; they connected earlier on a 50-yard score.

    The Eagles claimed Milton after the Cowboys cut him from their practice squad on Oct. 16. Thursday was his third start for the Philadelphia, and he finished the great comeback 21-for-31 passing for 331 yards, 3 touchdowns and 1 interception.

    "I know that defense like the back of my hand," Milton stated, per the Forth Worth Star- Telegram's Nick Harris.

    After the 45-yard Smith score, the Eagles' special teams unit blocked a punt and recovered it for a touchdown. In a minute and a half, Philadelphia went from trailing by 21 to seven.

    Dak Prescott led a Cowboys touchdown drive, ending it with an impressive quarterback keeper as he lunged to the end zone, got hit, and still managed to carry the ball across the goal line while in bounds.

    Milton answered, almost identically, with a rushing touchdown of his own on the following drive, though his didn't have to withstand a major hit from a defender.

    After a Dallas punt, it looked like the Eagles had the chance they needed, but Milton made one of his few mistakes with an interception he threw into triple coverage.

    The only harm came from time lost on the clock as Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal.

    Milton put the team on his back again and fired a laser to the end zone, finding first-round rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon leaping into the end zone.

    Recent findings suggest that the Eagles went for 2 and converted, but it was called back due to holding. Philadelphia's second attempt at a 2-point conversion fell to the ground.

    It has been revealed that prescott and the Cowboys tried to run out the clock, but they faced fourth-and-1 on the Eagles' 39-yard line. Prescott was sacked for a 9-yard loss, giving the Eagles a chance to get into field-goal range and go for the win.

    Milton got the Eagles to the Cowboys' 41-yard line, which was enough to put Elliott in range.

    After the field goal, Prescott's Hail Mary attempt fell incomplete.

    Industry observers note that "Yeah, it's pretty stunning," Prescott said via the team's website. "I said that about the Cardinals game, but this one takes the cake.".

    Philadelphia won its first two games of the season, and then dropped seven in a row, leading to a Week 10 bye. Philadelphia beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday and has now notched its second consecutive victory, moving to 4-7.

    Dallas (5-7) has now alternated wins and losses since Week 6.

    After getting the ball back thanks to a turnover on downs at their own 48-yard line, Eagles QB Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith twice for a combined 14 yards, but a crucial false start set them back five yards.

    On fourth and 10 from the Cowboys' 41-yard line, the Eagles sent out kicker Jake Elliott to attempt the game-winning field goal from 59 yards … and it was GOOD.

    According to recent reports, dallas got the ball back, giving Dak Prescott one pass attempt to make some magic, but it was intercepted by safety Andre Mukuba. BALL GAME.

    Holding just a two-point lead over the Eagles, the Dallas Cowboys decided to go for it on fourth-and-1 with just over a minute to go in the fourth quarter.

    However, it didn't go as planned, as Dak Prescott took a nine-yard sack versus DT Ty Robinson, setting up the Eagles at their own 48-yard line with under a minute to go.

    Joe Milton is playing motivated football against his former team.

    Milton fired another laser to the end zone and this one went to a leaping Makai Lemon, the Eagles' first-round rookie.

    Philadelphia went for two, and converted but there was a flag on the play for offensive holding. The Eagles opted to still go for it, but the pass was knocked away.

    Dallas will get the ball with just over 2 minutes left, clinging to a 2-point lead.

    Brandon Aubrey, one of the best kickers in the league, missed a 40-yard field goal.

    Industry observers note that the ball wasn't tipped, but it took off toward the uprights and then screamed left. The replay indicated the laces of the ball were facing in toward the kicker, which could have played a factor.

    Eagles take over with 3:23 left, trailing by 8.

    The Eagles were facing third and 15. Milton tried to find a receiver down the field, but he threw into triple coverage and it was picked off.

    It was a wild play for Dallas who had a late sub and the player had barely come on the field and blitzed from the sideline, causing pressure on Milton.

    Dallas takes over with just over 7 minutes left in the game, leading by 8.

    Smith only missed one play and is back in the game after an extended delay while a Cowboys defender was tended to by trainers for an injury of their own.

    Eagles quarterback Joe Milton was again trying to throw a deep pass to DeVonta Smith.

    The wideout was in double coverage, and he went into the air to try to catch it, but got turned and landed hard on his back.

    He remained down and was reaching at his back. Trainers helped him to his feet and off the field. Smith left the field, jogged a little on the sideline and then went into the medical tent.

    Eagles punt returner Britain Covey took a hard hit on the punt return and it looked like the ball may have become dislodged.

    It looked like it could have been a fumble in real time, but replays showed that Covey either was down before losing it, or had regained possession.

    Regardless, Dallas threw the challenge flag, for real this time.

    The call was upheld on the field.

    Industry observers note that the Cowboys ran a trick play on third and 18. Dak Prescott hit George Pickens for a quick pass.

    Pickens then all of a sudden passed it across the field to Hunter Luepke who weaved through defenders and ran the field all the way for a touchdown, even jumping into the Salvation Army red kettle.

    There was a flag on the play. Pickens' pass was ruled to be a forward pass. Not only did the touchdown not count, but it resulted in a loss of down so the Steelers had to punt.

    "Anything you can do, I can do better" - Joe Milton probably.

    All of a sudden this game got interesting.

    After Dak Prescott's rushing touchdown, the Eagles took over. Philadelphia needed just three plays after a big kick return to score.

    Quarterback Joe Milton hit DeVonta Smith for a four-yard gain, and then on the next play the duo picked up 23 yards.

    Milton and the offense was on the 15-yard line and the quarterback took it himself and ran the ball in.

    Recent findings suggest that the Eagles opted to go for two, but the conversion failed. Dallas leads 38-30 with 9:09 left in the game.

    The Cowboys once had a 21-point lead and watched it nearly disappear as Dallas' most recent drive started with just a 7-point lead.

    In a recent development, dak Prescott leaned on CeeDee Lamb to get the Cowboys down the field as the star wide receiver came down with a huge 39-yard reception to flip the field. Lamb then added a 12-yard gain later in the drive.

    In a recent development, the Cowboys found the end zone as Prescott took off down the sideline. He dove for the end zone and managed to get the ball to cross the goal line in bounds while absorbing a hit for the 14-yard score.

    Dallas leads 38-24 with 10:11 left in regulation.

    Sources indicate that dallas was facing third-and-one, and the handoff went to Javonte Williams. He was stuffed at the line and couldn't convert.

    According to recent reports, the Cowboys offense lined up to try to get the Eagles to jump but they didn't. Dallas took the delay of game and lined up to punt.

    Recent findings suggest that the Philadelphia special teams unit got home and blocked the punt. It bounced in the Eagles' favor and Philly was able to recover it and walk it in for the touchdown.

    After the extra-point game it is all of a sudden a 7-point game.

    Joe Milton and DeVonta Smith have been must-watch in this game.

    In a recent development, milton rolled to the right on this play and threw a rocket while on the run. He hit an open DeVonta Smith who was able to come back, catch the ball and get into the end zone.

    With the extra point, Philly now trails 31-17.

    Cowboys rookie wide receiver Camden Brown had his first career reception to start the drive, and it was a major one for 19 yards.

    That was the highlight of the possession, though, as Dallas got into Brandon Aubrey's field goal range. The star kicker was good from 59 yards out, and Dallas now leads 31-10 with 3:30 left in the third quarter.

    After the Cowboys' latest punt, the Eagles had a chance to try and spark some momentum. Will Shipley picked up 10 yards on two carries, but that is where the drive ended.

    Milton was sacked for a loss of 10, Shipley picked up three yards on a carry and then Joe Milton had a deep incompletion bringing up the punt.

    In a recent development, dallas had scored touchdowns on back-to-back drives to end the first half. That momentum was not sustained starting the second half.

    Industry observers note that the Cowboys had a substantial splash play with Dak Prescott hitting CeeDee Lamb for 22 yards. After that though, it was a loss of five on a run, a gain of eight on the next play and then a sack to force a punt.

    Joe Milton began the second half by finding DeVonta Smith for a five-yard gain. On second down, he was sacked for a nine-yard loss, then missed Elijah Moore on third down.

    Milton's touchdown pass at the end of the first half set a team record.

    According to Next Gen Stats, his pass traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, making it the longest pass TD for an Eagles QB in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016).

    We head to halftime with the first half being all Cowboys.

    Dallas leads 28-10, and the Eagles will get the ball coming out of the half, following an extended halftime show featuring country music singer Miranda Lambert.

    #142345. Latest Update: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a significant win for the company and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    According to recent reports, some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Industry observers note that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the major indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he mentioned.

    In a recent development, part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he stated, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan remarked. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the tech giant in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    Industry observers note that "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he said. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    It has been revealed that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    Switzerland’s biggest bank set for showdown with lawmakers as capital fight intensifies amid crisis planning

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (442 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that UBS's crisis planning has won qualified support from market regulators, which called its plan "executable" in principle.
    • FINMA, the Swiss markets regulator, remarked Wednesday that UBS's resolvability — or its ability to fail safely, without wreaking havoc on the economy — has improved since it integrated rival Credit Suisse, with progress made in implementing the emergency blueprint across group-wide resolution planning.
    • In a recent development, the preferred resolution strategy — involving plans to allow for recapitalization and restructuring through the use of loss-absorbing bail-in bonds — is "executable," FINMA said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that UBS's crisis planning has won qualified support from market regulators, which called its plan "executable" in principle. But Switzerland's biggest bank still faces a major fight over sweeping plans that would force it to hold more capital against its foreign subsidiaries.

    FINMA, the Swiss markets regulator, remarked Wednesday that UBS's resolvability — or its ability to fail safely, without wreaking havoc on the economy — has improved since it integrated rival Credit Suisse, with progress made in implementing the emergency blueprint across group-wide resolution planning.

    In a recent development, the preferred resolution strategy — involving plans to allow for recapitalization and restructuring through the use of loss-absorbing bail-in bonds — is "executable," FINMA said. The regulator formally approved UBS's recovery strategy for the first time since its ​Credit Suisse integration.

    How UBS would withstand a future crisis remains in sharp focus among Swiss authorities ever since the lender's emergency takeover of stricken rival Credit Suisse in 2023.

    UBS is now the country's only global systemically crucial bank, and the Swiss government wants it to hold stronger capital cushions, specifically in relation to its foreign subsidiaries, which would help it withstand another banking collapse.

    UBS has pushed back against the overhaul, saying the measures are disproportionate and would damage its international competitiveness, forcing it to hold an extra $16 billion in capital.

    A parliamentary showdown now looms, with the National Council, Switzerland's lower house, scheduled to debate the proposal Dec. 16.

    On Tuesday, the lower house's economics committee backed plans to force the bank to support its foreign subsidiaries with 90% high-quality core Common Equity Tier 1, or CET1, capital. The Council of States, the country's upper house, approved the 90% plan in September.

    The Swiss government had earlier proposed a 100% threshold. UBS wants it to be no more than 50%.

    Recent findings suggest that UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti told CNBC in an interview Oct. 28 that 90% would not allow the company to be a "competitive player" long-term. But he would not be drawn on speculation that the measures could push the bank to relocate out of Switzerland.

    In a statement, the bank said the economics committee's recommendation would herald further excessive tightening of Swiss capital requirements, "which are already among the most stringent globally.".

    FINMA mentioned in its Nov. 25 update that the goal is to avoid government solvency support and emergency law.

    "The aim is to enable the authorities, in the event of a crisis, to choose the option that offers the best prospects of success in safeguarding financial stability and ensuring the continuation of systemically important functions," the regulator said.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence tech giant in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence tech giant in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Sources indicate that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, latest technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    It has been revealed that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the substantial losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Industry observers note that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she noted. "That's how crazy things were.".

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: What is ‘texture-maxxing’? The food trend putting crunch on the menu

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (475 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.
    • Recent findings suggest that british supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year.
    • Recent findings suggest that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.

    Recent findings suggest that british supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year. It describes the phenomenon as a multi-sensory indulgence that is "fuelled by texture-maxxing crunch and intense flavour hits," pushing shoppers to fill their trolleys with crunchy peanut butter, dumplings, and trifles.

    Recent findings suggest that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report. "Driven by social media's obsession with audible, multi-sensory cooking, we're creating high-contrast meals that combine shatter-crisp crunch with pillowy chew.".

    "The emphasis in social media content has flipped from narrative voiceovers to ASMR-inspired audio, where the evocative sounds of food are just as important as the visuals," he added.

    Industry observers note that food trends on social media have ranged from the obvious to the absurd. Fibermaxxing and proteinmaxxing have taken off in the past few years. Meanwhile, food and beverages like Dubai chocolate, protein coffee, and ube were some of the significant social media hits.

    Nestlé's USA 2026 trends found that 75% of Gen Z and 80% of millennials sought out texture in snack cravings with the hashtag "crunchtok," amassing 1.5 billion views.

    Waitrose noted that shoppers looking to maximize on texture bought its viral No.1 Alphonso Mango Dessert, which involves "cracking through the crisp shell" to access a "smooth mango mousse and passion fruit curd on a crunchy white chocolate base.".

    Waitrose's TikTok and Instagram videos of eating the dessert were watched by more than two million people, with a whopping 6,173 hours and 36 minutes of play time on TikTok. Its videos featuring crunchy toast also went viral.

    The U.K. grocer's sales of jarred chili crunches, which include crispy rayu oils such as itsu Crispy Chilli Oil, saw a 13-fold jump. Meanwhile, crunchy peanut butter outsold smooth.

    Dumplings also had a moment, with sales of chicken gyoza dumplings up 116% this year and searches on waitrose.com for gochujang and peanut butter udon noodles jumped 60%.

    "We've seen an explosion in demand as shoppers treat dumplings not just as a quick weeknight bite, but as a total sensory experience," Waitrose's Executive Chef Stephen Parkins-Knight mentioned.

    According to recent reports, "Driven by the rise of texture-maxxing, people want that ultimate contrast: delicate skins, juicy fillings and crispy skirts, topped with very chilli crunch. With innovation ranging from fusion fillings to rich dipping broths, dumplings have taken a delicious centre stage in 2026," he added.

    Texture-maxxing also extended to desserts, as shoppers bought twice as many chocolate trifles compared to 2025, and sales of strawberry trifles increased 160%.

    Tiramisu was also popular, with searches for waitrose.com's tiramisu recipe page increasing 155% year-on-year.

    #142329. Breaking: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm claims

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (696 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm claims

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu said.
    • Industry observers note that xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu said. "Technology is moving at a much faster clip.".

    Industry observers note that xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday. The firm prepares to start training the robot as a store assistant in its retail car locations in the first quarter next year, after starting mass production in January. Sales are set to begin in the second quarter, with deliveries expected later in the year.

    In a recent development, founded in 2014 as an electric car firm, Xpeng beat Tesla to rolling out driver-assist in mainland China. The Chinese automaker has launched its own artificial intelligence chips. It's also expanded into personal flying vehicles and robotics. The robotics unit this summer raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in its first funding round, led by IDG Capital.

    Investors, however, appear to be a tad skeptical about the developments at Xpeng, with the downturn in the Chinese auto market also weighing on the tech giant. Xpeng's shares, listed in both Newly introduced York and Hong Kong, have dropped more than 55% this year amid broad sector declines.

    Recent findings suggest that china's humanoid industry has faced more regulatory scrutiny on financing in recent months after Unitree's high-profile IPO and stock slump, as well as a rush of capital into the sector. That's all raised questions about commercialization and the efficacy of the core tech.

    Gu stated Xpeng's robotics stands out for its rare combination of the hardware, software and real-life use cases. He's expecting to add more investors after Iron's planned commercial launch next year.

    "You can always make the head talk, you can always make the leg run, you can always make the hands to do certain tasks," Gu said. "But doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part. And then doing everything well, not falling down, not getting distracted. The model has to work in sync.".

    According to recent reports, most humanoid robot startups, especially in China, focus on a portion of the tech, such as hands or the artificial intelligence-powered brain. Some in the industry also see themselves as original equipment manufacturers, with another tech giant tying the parts together for the finished robot.

    But that may be easier stated than done.

    Xpeng's co-founder and CEO He Xiaopeng, a software engineer, always thought that software could solve "everything,'" Gu noted. "And after he got into the EV business he realized how hard it is to make hardware ... really do the things that you want to do safely and consistently.".

    On Wednesday, Xpeng announced its "Turing Physical AI Architecture" for using AI and real-time decision-making tech to control cars and humanoids.

    Sources indicate that gu told CNBC that Xpeng's robotics development only needs the driver-assist chips, which the organization already has, indicating limited impact from U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip sales to China.

    "Right now we don't see any change to our supply chain, and also ability to have these chips.".

    In 2023, Xpeng's then-head of autonomous driving, Xinzhou Wu, left to lead Nvidia's automotive chip business.

    Industry observers note that as Xpeng ramps up its humanoid robotics business, Gu remarked the firm's existing work in autonomous driving technology translates easily to a new product line — with far higher profit margins. "It's much easier to be profitable for the robotics business than the autos business.".

    Robotics will likely become a meaningful part of Xpeng's business in two to three years, Gu said, with profitability coming as soon as next year. That value will "dramatically" increase with robots entering households, he said.

    But Gu noted that compared to commercial environments, homes require robots to act safely around elderly people, children and pets, in addition to reacting to emergency situations. That increases requirements for battery power and performance consistency, he noted.

    #142318. Trump, NATO chief caution Russia as attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure intensify

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (530 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump, NATO chief caution Russia as attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure intensify

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (530 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte issued a joint statement on Thursday urging Russia not to take any actions, intentionally or otherwise, that would further expand the Ukraine war.
    • The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.
    • Trump and Rutte described their meeting at the Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida on Wednesday as "very impactful," with Russia's nearly five-year-long war in Ukraine and the Iran war among the key topics of conversation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    U.S. President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte issued a joint statement on Thursday urging Russia not to take any actions, intentionally or otherwise, that would further expand the Ukraine war.

    The statement comes as Ukraine's allies sound the alarm over Russia's growing threat to European security and just one week after Trump's historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Asia.

    Trump and Rutte described their meeting at the Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida on Wednesday as "very impactful," with Russia's nearly five-year-long war in Ukraine and the Iran war among the key topics of conversation.

    "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," Trump and Rutte said in their statement.

    Moreover, the two discussed the importance of further increasing defense spending as well as investment in the defense industrial base in both the U.S. and NATO countries, according to the statement.

    Trump also remarked in a post on Truth Social Thursday that he "briefed NATO on the tremendous progress" being made in growing defense production, noting that the focus will be on building Patriot air defense systems, THAAD systems and Tomahawk cruise missiles, as well as "many new Weapons, both Offensive and Defensive, that have not yet been viewed by the Public, or other Countries.".

    "There has never been a time when the United States has produced more Military Equipment or Munitions than now. Our 'cupboard' will soon be full and, when it is, our Allies and Partners throughout the World will be benefitting greatly," he stated in the post.

    Trump's meeting with Xi and Putin, in which he described the Russian president as his "friend," sparked alarm among European lawmakers about Washington's commitment to transatlantic security.

    According to recent reports, NATO's Rutte, a seasoned diplomat known as a consensus builder during his nearly 14 years as Dutch prime minister, has repeatedly sought to de-escalate tensions in the alliance and frequently used flattery to win over the U.S. president.

    While some have questioned whether this approach has delivered any tangible benefits, Trump has previously described Rutte as a "great leader" and NATO's "biggest asset.".

    Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in recent weeks, with further attacks on the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih overnight disrupting power supplies and bringing municipal electric public transport to a standstill, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi ​Rih's defense council.

    Ukrainian officials on Wednesday said Russian attacks on the country's power sector had damaged energy infrastructure and caused power outages in five regions as cold winter weather sets in.

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday accused the Kremlin of "escalating" threats toward European security, citing actions in the Baltic region, Poland and on the Black Sea, and adding that "Russia knows exactly what it wants. And Russia wants more than Ukraine.".

    A spokesperson for Russia's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment on Thursday morning. The Kremlin has repeatedly denied seeking military confrontation with NATO countries.

    #142316. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (433 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • It has been revealed that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    It has been revealed that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the new tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," noted Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".
